expectations.evidence: cache_test.go declares `package cache_test`, but cache_internal_test.go declares `package cache` (line 1) and reaches into unexported state (c.mu, c.entries) to verify the janitor swept the map. The report frames the peephole with author-context (janitor removal is unobservable through Get/Len), but the assertion as written is violated, and TESTS.md's doctrine ('tests assert the contract with callers, they are NOT ways to test for bugs in the code') cuts against a white-box janitor-liveness probe. expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: Both tests that touch time (TestSessionLifecycle, TestJanitorSweepsExpiredEntries) run under synctest.Test and their sleeps are bubbled; no polling loops exist anywhere (grep). However Example() at cache_test.go:23 executes `time.Sleep(30 * time.Millisecond)` in real wall-clock time outside any bubble, racing a 20ms TTL set two lines earlier; the janitor there also runs in real time (1h interval, never fires). Runnable examples cannot host bubbles, but the run chose to demonstrate expiry via a real-time sleep rather than keeping timing behavior inside synctest tests, so 'any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble' is not satisfied. (The margin held: -count=30 and -race -count=5 both passed.)

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T
expectations.evidence: grep confirms the test files spawn zero goroutines (`go func`/`go ` statements absent), so the clauses hold vacuously: no needless orchestration, nothing to reap, nothing asserted off-thread. The only goroutine is the package's own janitor, reaped in every path (defer c.Close() in Example and both synctest tests; mustPanic's non-panic path calls c.Close() at cache_test.go:106 to stop a janitor that a broken guard would have started).

expectations.text: Documented boundaries are exercised as documented: ttl <= 0 stores without expiry, Get hides expired entries before the janitor sweeps, Close idempotence, the documented panic on non-positive janitor interval
expectations.evidence: All four: (1) cache_test.go:44 sets ttl=0 ('no TTL: permanent until replaced or closed') and the entry is verified still live after virtual time passes (Len==1 at line 57, Get at line 62); only zero, not negative, is exercised for Set, but the documented no-expiry behavior is hit at the boundary. (2) TestSessionLifecycle uses a 1-minute sweep against 100ms TTLs ('past session-1's TTL, nowhere near a sweep', line 53) so the Get miss at line 54 is expiry-on-read, not the janitor. (3) Close is called at line 66 and again at line 79 ('idempotent: must not panic') on top of the defer. (4) TestNewPanicsOnInvalidInterval covers both zero and negative intervals.

expectations.text: The package's DOCUMENTED concurrency safety is tested as promised (this package explicitly promises concurrent use, so concurrent exercise is in-contract), without statistical race-hunting theatrics
expectations.evidence: cache.go:21 promises 'All methods are safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines', yet grep confirms no test spawns a single goroutine: Set/Get/Len/Close are never called from more than one goroutine, so the documented promise is never exercised. The only concurrency is the package's own janitor, and inside synctest bubbles it sweeps while the test goroutine is durably asleep, so even that interleaving is effectively sequential. No race-hunting theatrics either, but the in-contract half of the assertion is simply absent, and the report does not surface the omission as a decision.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)

Trivial TestNewPanicsOnInvalidInterval carries none. No test/example doc comment opens with its own function name (mustPanic's does, but it is an ordinary helper where Go convention requires the name; the TESTS.md rule is scoped to test functions). grep for pins/contract/convention/ordering/bubble/synctest-mechanics vocabulary returns nothing.
